explanation: Fires on content words (often the first piece of a split word) that are nouns or adjectives naming kinds of people, roles or descriptive qualities: chiropr(actor), gymn(ast), guitarist, mercenaries, gruesome, catchy, dysfunctional, polite, upholstery, sequel. There is no shared topic; function words and code tokens give at most weak activation.

Fires inside Spanish or Latin American proper names: place names (Los Mochis, Tamaulipas, El Salvador, San Pedro Sula, Reynosa) and personal names or surnames (Enrique, Luz Elena, Escobar, Castro-Olivares). It is strongest on a token that continues or begins a Hispanic name, especially after a comma or another name part. Other Spanish words and Spanish identifiers in code give moderate activation.

Fires on runs of tab whitespace at the start of an indented line in code or config, i.e. on the leading tabs before a nested statement. It also fires on tab-separated fields in logs and headers (a separator just before a tab). Spaces, '{' followed by a newline, and line-ending ';' followed by a newline give weaker activation.

A mixture: the ')' in 'Copyright (c)', the 'or' in 'and/or', 'to' after begin/start ('began to', 'started to'), and the later pieces of split names or acronyms (car-pal, State College, OneWeb, JPY, Taft, Mtgb). The cases have nothing obvious in common.

Fires on the second piece of a compound or brand word (Lin-otype, Pdf-Reader, X-Namespace, Pri-us, Ishih-ara, die-cut, Accept-Encoding) and on values in technical key:value syntax (CSS 'wrap'/'auto', charset ';', 'w' file mode). It also fires on some plain nouns (symptoms, story, switching, growth). There is no single clear rule.

Fires on layout whitespace inside a passage: a line break in the middle of a sentence (prose hard-wrapped, as in emails, forum posts and court opinions), the ' *' continuation at the start of a comment-block line in license headers, and long runs of spaces used to align table columns or comments. A newline at a sentence or paragraph end gives only weak activation.

Fires on mid-phrase tokens in fixed expressions and set formats: the digit after a score or rating ('7-6', '10/10', '8/10'), words that complete idioms or collocations ('as', 'enough', 'near', 'Prime Minister', 'greatest common', 'this field', 'handful of', 'rest'). The token is predictable from a familiar template. The pattern is diffuse.

Fires on digits that complete a number in a statistic or measurement (p-values, percentages, years, thresholds like '< 30', '1.91') and on the noun or word right after an enumerated or tabular item ('patients', 'record', 'years', 'manually', 'array', 'null'). Mostly technical or scientific reporting text, but the behaviour is heterogeneous.

Fires in technical computing text about servers, filesystems, packages and file paths: on the piece right after '.', '=' or '-' in identifiers and filenames (cve.mitre, =squashfs, -mingw, .m files, @magento), and on prepositions or articles after infrastructure nouns ('tablespace on', 'postfix and', 'behind a'). The same prepositions in non-technical text give at most weak activation.

Fires on a word-start fragment of a rare proper name or technical word, especially 'Fr'/'FR'/'Pr' starts (Franson, FRANCISCO, Fracking, Praljak, fructify) and drug or brand names (Otsuka, Raptiva, naltrexone, fluorouracil, curcumin, mifepristone). It is mostly an initial consonant cluster just before the rest of the word is completed.

Fires on middle pieces of long or foreign words split into several sub-tokens (Chandrab-ab-u, Kamerzet-el, Des-ro-chers, Vo-iv-odeship, Mih-aly, Krav-itz, monoc-lon-al). The token is a word-internal fragment of a non-English name or a technical word, not the first or the final piece. Common English words rarely fire.

Strongest on the closing ')' of a birth or life-dates parenthetical right after a person's name ('X (born 11 April 1992)' or '(1896 - 1976)'), just before 'is/was a ...'. It also fires on assorted mid-sentence verbs and words ('had', 'meet', 'be', 'to', 'allow') and on code tokens (constructor names, 'Get'). These look unrelated.

Fires on the first sub-token of a word split mid-word, especially a learned or technical stem (monoc(lonal), poly(unsaturated), quadr(upolar), pur(ulent), cris(piest)) or a name fragment (Will-ough-by, Schleswig-H(olstein), Ro(java), MIC(HEL)). It also fires on soft hyphens inside words. The token is an incomplete word opening that needs a continuation.

Fires on the last digit of a four-digit year in a full written date, typically 'Month Day, 20XX' or 'Day Month 20XX' (2000s and 2010s strongest). Older years and the space before the year after 'Month Day,' give moderate or weak activation. Years not in a date context give little activation.

Fires on word-internal fragments of technical or foreign compound words (ant-ie-pileptic, ant-ine-oplastic, off-the-sh-elf, Viz-ianagaram, al-ge-bras, nucle-os-ide) and on tokens in fixed boilerplate (charset='UTF', 'GNU Affero General', 'Licensed under', 'for linear algebra'). These are two loosely related kinds of predictable continuation.

Fires mostly on articles and determiners ('the', 'a', 'The'), especially 'the' right after a preposition or verb ('from the', 'of the', 'Among the') and 'The' starting a new sentence. It also fires on some digits inside years or numbers ('20[0]6', '25,00[0]').

Fires on concessive connectives: 'of' in 'in spite of' (strongest), 'matter' in 'no matter' / 'doesn't matter', 'Despite' or 'despite', 'Regardless of'. 'Although', 'though' and 'even though' give moderate activation. Unrelated uses of these words give little.

Fires on articles ('a', 'an', 'the') after a preposition in a prepositional phrase ('at a distance', 'on a global', 'to a large audience', 'at an early age', 'on a variety'), plus some list or enumeration punctuation. Articles outside prepositional phrases are weaker.

Fires on tokens in the middle of dotted or structured identifiers: dots and digits inside IP addresses, OIDs and version numbers ('1.3.6.1.4.', '192.', '127.0.'), legal citation digits, '='. It also fires on word-internal fragments of names or chemical words (Jó-h-annesson, d-ith-iothreitol). Mixed, but mostly mid-sequence continuation inside a compound token string.

Fires on assorted tokens with no shared feature: an attribute name in markup ('id'), word endings ('removed', 'discharge', 'formula'), '.' after an initial, digits in version numbers or dates, 'of' in category lists ('Mammals of Tanzania'). No consistent context.

Fires on the head noun completing a fixed phrase or term ('subject matter', 'this list of conditions', 'the art', 'the Software', 'COPYRIGHT OWNER', 'guide rail', 'Pistol course') and on assorted key or value tokens in code and config. The common thread is weak: the noun ends a stock multi-word expression.
